LZ4 1.10.0, the block format's reference implementation (lz4.c, lz4hc.c).

Upstream:  https://github.com/lz4/lz4
Release:   v1.10.0 (2024-07-22)
Tarball:   https://github.com/lz4/lz4/archive/refs/tags/v1.10.0.tar.gz
           SHA-256 537512904744b35e232912055ccf8ec66d768639ff3abe5788d90d792ec5f48b
           (the same digest Homebrew's lz4 1.10.0 formula pins)
Copied:    lib/lz4.c, lib/lz4.h, lib/lz4hc.c, lib/lz4hc.h, lib/LICENSE
           -> this directory (unmodified)
Licence:   LICENSE (BSD 2-Clause) for everything copied.
Not copied: the frame format (lz4frame.*), xxhash, lz4file, the programs:
           fn stores LZ4 BLOCKS inside its own record frame
           (books/payload-lz-record.lisp), so neither the frame format nor its
           checksum is used.

Role: an UNTRUSTED encoder.  fn calls it only to produce a candidate block for
a record's payload span (host/native/fn-lz4.c, host/native/lz4.lisp); ACL2's
proved decoder (books/payload-lz.lisp fn-lz-decode) checks the candidate
decodes to exactly the span before the record is taken
(books/payload-lz-append.lisp fn-lzr-append-decide), and every read decodes
through ACL2.  No vendored decoder is called.

Refresh: fetch the release tarball, check its SHA-256 against the release's
published digest, re-copy the same five files, update the lines above and the
digests below, rebuild (tools/build_lz4.sh) and rerun
tests/acl2/payload-lz-append-tests.lisp's real blocks and
tests/test_lz4_candidate.py.
